memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The name of the Israelite who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a Simeonite family. And the name of the Midianite woman who was put to death was Kozbi daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a Midianite family. - Num 25:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Scripture pauses to name the two who were put to death: Zimri, a leader among the Simeonites, and Kozbi, the daughter of a Midianite chief. These were not obscure, unknown figures but people of standing and influence. Their names and positions are recorded for the memory of Israel.

There is a sobering point in this detail. Zimri was a leader, someone others looked to. His sin was not hidden but public, committed openly before the whole assembly. Those in positions of influence bear a greater weight, for their sin affects and misleads many. Leadership does not exempt anyone from accountability before God.

We might also notice that sin is not anonymous to God. Every act is known and named before Him. We sometimes imagine our sins are hidden or forgotten, but nothing escapes God's sight. He knows us fully, including the things we would rather keep in the dark.

This truth could terrify us, but in Christ it becomes a comfort. The God who knows our sin completely has provided complete forgiveness for those who come to Him. Nothing is hidden from His eyes, yet in Jesus, our sins are covered and remembered no more (Heb 8:12). Bring your hidden things into His light, and find mercy there.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as though your sins are hidden, or known to God?
2. How does greater influence bring greater responsibility before God?
3. What comfort do you find in a God who knows you fully yet forgives?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know me completely, and nothing is hidden from Your sight. Thank You that in Christ my sins are forgiven and remembered no more. Draw me to walk honestly in Your light. Amen.
